features.description: harness start and harness queue add refuse a --spec (or SPEC_FILES) path absent from the project's origin/main (or --base) before anything is queued or started; a resume and a --brief-only start are not checked.
steps:
A function `spec_missing …` exists in `lib/config.sh` or a new `lib/spec.sh` (one-line usage header; sourced by `bin/harness` and `lib/queue.sh`): it runs `git -C

fetch -q origin` (a failed fetch is one line on stderr and the check reads the last fetched ref), tests each path with `git cat-file -e :`, and for the first path not in the ref prints `spec : not in (fetched now); commit and push it, or name its ref with --base` and returns 1; every path present returns 0 and prints nothing

In `bin/harness` `cmd_start`, the check runs before the first `queue_add` (the busy-project and `MAX_PARALLEL_RUNS` paths queue before the worktree exists), with the `--spec` value split on spaces as `SPEC_FILES` is, or with `SPEC_FILES` from the project's `.harness/config.sh` when no `--spec` is given, the ref `--base` when given else `origin/$MAIN_BRANCH`; a miss is `die` with the line (exit 1); a run id whose worktree `$WT_ROOT/<project>/<run>` exists (a resume) and a `--brief` with no spec are not checked; `cmd_queue add` (not `add --continue`) runs the same check before `queue_add`

Checks in a new `tests/checks/83-spec-must-exist.sh` (written first and watched failing; each name one line in `tests/fixtures/check-names.txt`, `LC_ALL=C sort -c tests/fixtures/check-names.txt` prints nothing): `harness start

--spec docs/missing.md` exits 1, prints `spec docs/missing.md: not in origin/main`, and makes no worktree under `$T/wt`, no state dir under `$T/state` and no `.args` file under `$T/state/queue`; the same file committed in the stub project but not pushed is refused the same way; pushed, the start proceeds and the stub run's worktree exists; `--spec "a.md b.md"` with only `b.md` missing names `b.md`

More checks in `tests/checks/83-spec-must-exist.sh`: `--base ` with the spec on that branch only proceeds, and the same without `--base` is refused naming `origin/main`; `SPEC_FILES=docs/missing.md` in the stub's `.harness/config.sh` with no `--spec` is refused; `--brief "x"` alone with no `SPEC_FILES` is not checked and starts; `harness start

` of an existing run worktree is not checked (a `docs/missing.md` in its `run.env` does not refuse the resume); `harness queue add

--spec docs/missing.md` prints the line, exits 1 and leaves no `.args` file in `$T/state/queue`; `harness queue add

--spec SPEC.md` (present) prints `queued:`

`journal/decisions/2026-10-31-spec-must-exist.md` exists with title, provenance, then finding · choice · rejected: the reference is the project's `origin/main` (marked *default*) and not the working tree, with the rejected alternatives the spec lists (the working tree as the reference; checking only at `queue add`; failing the runner's start and leaving the entry in `done/`; the initializer guessing from the title); the runner's part is left for Q1-02 to add in place
`bash -n bin/harness lib/queue.sh` and `bash -n` on every other shell file the feature touched print nothing; `git diff origin/main -- lib/queue.sh` is empty (the runner's re-check is Q1-02)
the suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing (`N/M checks passed`, no `FAIL` line)

features.description: The queue runner re-checks a start entry's spec at dequeue and parks the entry in queue/held/ with the line instead of starting it, then goes on to the next entry; README, architecture and the decision file describe the refusal and the park; an Opus subagent reviews the Q1 diff.
steps: In `lib/queue.sh`, after the entry is chosen and before the `mv` to `done/`: for a `start` entry with `--spec` in its `.args` (decoded as the runner decodes them: one argument per line, a newline as `\x1f`) or whose project `.harness/config.sh` names `SPEC_FILES`, `spec_missing` runs with the entry's `--base` if any; on a miss the entry is moved to `queue/held/` with a `.why` beside it holding the line and the time (the shape `harness queue park` writes: `<line> (<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>)`), one `parked <entry>: spec <path>: not in <ref> …` line goes to `runner.log`, no run starts, and the loop continues with the next entry

Checks in `tests/checks/83-spec-must-exist.sh` (written first and watched failing; names in `tests/fixtures/check-names.txt`): an entry queued with the spec present, then a pushed commit that deletes the file from `origin/main` (no rewrite), and the runner started with `harness queue start`: the entry's `.args` is in `$T/state/queue/held/`, its `.why` holds `spec <path>: not in origin/main`, `runner.log` has a `parked` line, no state dir for that run exists, and a second entry (a `--brief` start of the same project, or another project) is started by the same runner; an `.args` planted by hand in `$T/state/queue` naming `docs/missing.md` is parked at dequeue the same way; `harness queue list` shows the parked entry with `not in origin/main` in its reason

`journal/decisions/2026-10-31-spec-must-exist.md` gains the runner's re-check and park in place (the choice: park, never start; *default* no notification, the runner's log and `harness queue list` carry it); `README.md`'s `harness start` and `harness queue` rows say that a `--spec` path absent from `origin/main` (or `--base`) is refused at once and parked at dequeue; `docs/architecture.md` §3 (`bin/harness`, `lib/queue.sh` rows), §7 (the guard table: a missing spec parks, never starts) and §12 (the runner's dequeue) say the same

`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- bin lib tests > $HARNESS_SCRATCH/Q1.diff`; an Opus subagent reads that file with the brief: the order of the spec check against the two early `queue_add` paths in `cmd_start`, that a resume and a `--brief`-only start skip it, and that the runner's park leaves the loop able to start the next entry; its Critical and Important findings are fixed RED→GREEN and listed in the entry's `verified_how` (one round; a second only after a Critical finding)
`bash -n bin/harness lib/queue.sh` and `bash -n` on every other shell file the milestone touched print nothing
the suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing (`N/M checks passed`, no `FAIL` line)

No code change.

features.description: lib/record.sh's F memoizes its pure answers per process, keyed on the subcommand, the list file's content hash and the other arguments, never on mtime, path or time; a node shim in a new check file proves one node start for repeated calls and a new start after one byte changes.
steps: A new `tests/checks/84-node-memo.sh` (written first and watched failing; names in `tests/fixtures/check-names.txt`) puts a `node` shim first on `PATH` that appends one line per exec (its arguments and whether `HARNESS_LANE` is set) to a count file and execs the real node, as `tests/stub-claude.sh` stands in for `claude`; a check that sources `lib/record.sh` with `HARNESS_HOME=$HH` shows: two `F model opus` calls start node once and print the same model id; `F summary` twice on one `feature_list.json` fixture starts node once; after one byte of the list changes (a `passes` flipped), `F summary` starts node again and prints the new count; the list restored to its first content answers from the memo without a start (content, not mtime)

In `lib/record.sh`, `F` keeps a bash associative array for the subcommands `docs/plans/2026-11-03-C1-suite-cpu.md` names as pure: `model:<alias>` for `model`; `<sub>:<sha1 of the list file>:<other args>` for `summary` and the other list readers, the hash by `sha1sum` or `git hash-object`; a key miss runs node and stores stdout and the exit code; a hit prints the stored stdout and returns the stored exit code; the memo lives in the process only (no file under the state dir, scratch or cache), and the subcommands the plan lists as not memoized (`append`, `ingest`, `render`, `pack`, `insert`, `repair`, `notify`, and `unpark` when it printed an id) call node every time

`inbox.mjs answers` in `answers_hash` (`lib/record.sh`) is memoized on `INBOX.md`'s content hash the same way when the plan lists it in the top five; `git diff origin/main -- lib/*.sh | grep '^[-+].*note "'` prints nothing (no `harness-log.md` note text changes)

`journal/decisions/2026-10-31-fewer-node-starts.md` gains under *Choice* the memo (the key's shape, which subcommands, marked *default*) and under *Rejected* a disk cache of node answers (a stale answer outlives the process; the invariant of `decisions/2026-10-30-partial-key`) and keying on mtime or path
`bash -n lib/record.sh` and `bash -n` on every other shell file touched print nothing; `node --check lib/features.mjs` prints nothing
the suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing (`N/M checks passed`, no `FAIL` line)

features.description: The coordinator's end check asks features.mjs its five questions in one node start (F poll), the lane loop's next and milestone-done the same where they sit in one iteration, check.sh's two treekey calls become one, and date/cat become bash builtins in lib/ where the plan's table puts them in the top five; an idle poll starts node at most once per iteration.
steps: `lib/features.mjs` gains a `poll <list> <att> <max> <parked> [<lane>]` subcommand that prints, as labelled lines (`summary\t…`, `parked\t…`, `blocked\t…`, `next\t…`, `milestone-done\t…` or the names the session chooses), what `summary`, `parked`, `blocked`, `next` and `milestone-done` print for the same arguments, as a composition of the same exported functions; a unit check in `tests/checks/84-node-memo.sh` (`node --input-type=module -e`, written first) compares its lines with the five subcommands' output on a fixture list with one parked and one blocked feature; the five subcommands stay

`lib/driver.sh`'s end check (the `! opened && alive == 0` branch) reads `F poll` once with `mapfile` instead of its separate `F summary`, `F parked`, `F blocked` and `F next` calls, and `lib/lane.sh`'s loop uses one `F poll` (or the memo) where `F next` and `F milestone-done` sit in one iteration; `lib/check.sh`'s `treekey.mjs --partial` and `--names` calls become one node start when both are needed; `date` and `cat` in `lib/*.sh` become `$EPOCHSECONDS`, `printf '%(%F %T)T'` and `$(< file)` only where `docs/plans/2026-11-03-C1-suite-cpu.md` lists them in the top five, and never in `tests/`

A check in `tests/checks/84-node-memo.sh` runs a stub run with the shim on `PATH`, `MAX_LANES=2` in the stub project's `.harness/config.sh`, one lane held open on a barrier (`stub_wait`/`stub_go`) and nothing left to open, over a window of at least 5 polls (`HARNESS_LANE_POLL=1`): the shim's count of node starts without `HARNESS_LANE` set during the window is at most the number of polls the window holds (counted from `run.log`'s poll-paced lines or a `log` line the driver already writes), so an idle poll starts node at most once

`git diff origin/main -- lib/*.sh | grep '^[-+].*note "'` prints nothing (no `harness-log.md` note text changes); every existing check that compares `harness-log.md` or `run.log` lines passes unchanged

`journal/decisions/2026-10-31-fewer-node-starts.md` gains under *Choice* the poll subcommand, the treekey merge and the builtins (each marked *default*), and under *Rejected* rewriting the `.mjs` helpers in bash and a long-lived node server the driver talks to

features.description: One full run per coding session, last: the coding prompt's suite rule and §3 order change, lane.sh passes suite_runs and suite_full to the coding row of metrics.jsonl, and summary.mjs reports `Suite runs` (full per coding session) in harness report and summary.json.
steps: Checks in `tests/checks/79-suite-length.sh` (written first and watched failing; names in `tests/fixtures/check-names.txt`): a stub run's rendered `prompt-coding.md` has `once, last, after your final edit of any file` and `TEST_JOBS=2` with `slower and as flaky`, and in its §3 the `## Gotchas` step's text comes before the suite step's (line order); `prompts/coding.md` no longer has `Run it in full once before you flip`

`prompts/coding.md`'s *The suite* ground rule reads: while iterating pass arguments for a subset; run it in full once, last, after the final edit of any file, `CLAUDE.md` included (a full run before that is paid twice); a red check that check.sh reran green is a flake it has already recorded, never rerun the suite by hand for it, a red after its rerun is real; never lower the suite's parallelism to make room for other lanes (`TEST_JOBS=2` on this box: slower and as flaky, 2026-10-28; `decisions/2026-10-29-check-timeout-25m`); the timeout clause stays; §3 *Finish* puts the `## Gotchas` step before the full-run step with one sentence saying why (`so the tree you tested is the tree that ends the session`), `entry.json` and the commit after

Checks in `tests/checks/77-leftovers.sh` or a new `tests/checks/85-suite-runs.sh` (written first): a stub run whose session makes two full `check.sh` calls and one subset call has a coding row in `metrics.jsonl` with `suite_runs` 3 and `suite_full` 2 and the `suite ran 3x` note as before; a session with no call has `0` and `0`; `summary.json`'s `suite_runs` is `{ sessions, full, runs, full_per_session }` with `full_per_session` 2 for a run of one such session; `harness report --md` prints `Suite runs | 2 full per coding session (2 in 1; 3 runs in all)` after the `Flakes` row and the TTY view the same row; the rendered `prompt-retro.md` carries the number; a run with no coding row prints `0`

`lib/lane.sh` counts the session's `check-runs.log` rows between `t0` and `t1` whose kind is `full` beside the existing count and passes `suite_runs` and `suite_full` as two more trailing arguments to `MET append`; `lib/metrics.mjs` `metricsRow` writes them on the coding row (`null` when the log is missing); `lib/summary.mjs` builds `suite_runs` from the coding rows and `reportRows` gains the `Suite runs` row; `git diff origin/main -- lib/lane.sh | grep '^[-+].*note "'` prints nothing (the note's text is unchanged); `trends` is unchanged

`journal/decisions/2026-10-31-one-full-run.md` exists with title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected (a driver-enforced cap on full runs per session; counting from `harness-log.md`'s note; the rule in `CLAUDE.md` alone), the `TEST_JOBS=2` sentence's place in the shared prompt marked *default*
`bash -n lib/lane.sh` prints nothing; `node --check lib/metrics.mjs lib/summary.mjs` prints nothing; `LC_ALL=C sort -c tests/fixtures/check-names.txt` prints nothing
the suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing (`N/M checks passed`, no `FAIL` line)
